text:
laura: thinking about rolling out rwd-13b-q8 as a cost-optimized variant. proposing staged rollout + a small holdback group to catch regressions. initial plan: 3% traffic, 0.5% holdback, 24h observation. thoughts? :thinking_face:
ajay: curious which eval sets you want to prioritize. long-form summarization and multi-turn QA historically hit quantized models harder. would like to surface per-slice diffs not just global accuracy.
laura: good call. prioritize: 1) multi-turn QA (prod prompt set), 2) summarization 800-1500 tokens, 3) cost/latency slices.
evals-bot: quick snapshot (baseline=rwd-13b-fp16 vs candidate=rwd-13b-q8) on seeded evals:
```
- overall answer_accuracy: baseline=87.2%, candidate=86.0% (−1.2pp)
- multi-turn QA: baseline=84.6%, candidate=82.7% (−1.9pp)
- long-summaries (rouge-L): baseline=41.8, candidate=40.5 (−1.3)
- p95 latency: baseline=220ms, candidate=232ms (+12ms)
- error rate (model errors / requests): baseline=0.12%, candidate=0.18%
- tokens/unit-cost: candidate ~18% cheaper in our cost model
```
ajay: two notes: a 1.9pp drop on multi-turn QA is notable. but +12ms p95 is fine. we should gate on absolute and relative thresholds and on per-slice regression.
oleg: infra note: q8 runs have slightly higher memory locality which can spike OOMs at certain batch sizes. I recommend we restrict batch cap to 8 for the initial rollout and enable OOM logging hooks.
maria: what are the exact rollback triggers? product needs clear SLOs to approve traffic.
ajay: proposal for automatic fallback triggers (candidate -> full rollback to baseline):
```
- any per-slice metric drop > 1.5 percentage points (absolute) on critical slices (multi-turn QA, safety-check)
- OR overall answer_accuracy drop > 1.0pp
- OR p95 latency increase > 50ms (absolute)
- OR error rate increase > 0.5% (absolute)
- OR two OOMs on the rollout pool within 30m
- observation window: 15m rolling, require 3 consecutive windows to trigger auto-fallback
```
laura: that seems conservative but reasonable. can we make the per-slice rule opt-in for rollout so we can tune without full rollback for first 6h? maybe mark as alert-only then escalate to auto-fallback if persists.
ajay: yes -- alert for first 6h, then auto-fallback enabled after 6h if the regression persists.
oleg: I'll add batch cap and OOM hooks. infra-bot will also create a transient pool tagged `q8-canary-1887654321` and limit concurrency.
infra-bot: scheduled: create pool `q8-canary-1887654321` (gpus: a100s-small), batch_cap:8, start_time: now + 10m, healthchecks enabled. :rocket:
laura: rollout policy draft (for config):
```
rollout: {
  traffic_split: "3%",
  holdback: "0.5%",
  observation_window: "24h",
  initial_phase: {
    duration: "6h",
    per_slice_fallback: "alert-only"
  },
  after_initial: {
    per_slice_fallback: "auto",
    auto_fallback_rules: ["answer_accuracy","p95_latency","error_rate","oom_count"]
  }
}
```
maria: please also attach a short guardrail checklist for support to run in case of user reports (quick compare script, how to reroute traffic manually).
ajay: I'll add an eval job to run high-sensitivity adversarial prompt set every 10m and push to the dashboard. if adj. accuracy drops by >1.5pp on that set, immediate alert.
evals-bot: scheduling periodic eval job: `rwd-q8-canary-adversarial` every 10m, results streaming to /dashboard/canaries/1887654321.
laura: ok let's go. start at T+10m with 3% traffic / 0.5% holdback, batch_cap=8. monitor first 6h as alert-only for per-slice diffs, enable auto-fallback after.
infra-bot: acknowledged. starting rollout in 10m. :eyes:
(about 45m later)
evals-bot: initial A/B from live traffic (first 45m):
- overall answer_accuracy: baseline=87.1%, candidate=86.2% (−0.9pp)
- multi-turn QA: baseline=84.5%, candidate=82.9% (−1.6pp)
- long-summaries: baseline rougel=41.6, candidate=40.9 (−0.7)
- p95 latency: baseline=221ms, candidate=233ms (+12ms)
- error rate: baseline=0.11%, candidate=0.17%
ajay: multi-turn still −1.6pp but within our alert threshold for now (alert-only). watch the adversarial set.
maria: product approves continuing to 24h but want to check retention of edge cases at 6h and 24h.
oleg: infra: no OOMs observed, CPU/GPU usage stable.
laura: thanks all. next checkpoint @ 6h mark unless any auto-fallback triggers. :thumbsup:
